title: Toward a Perceptual Theory of Transparency

findings.antecedent: mean luminance of the central disk in matching display (Lmean)
findings.mechanism: visual system integrates mean luminance and range to assign transmittance
findings.quote: transmittance matches are almost perfectly fit by increasing linear functions that pass through the origin.

findings.antecedent: Michelson contrast within the target disk
findings.consequent: slope of linear fit for transmittance matches
findings.mechanism: visual system integrates contrast and mean luminance to assign transmittance
findings.quote: as the contrast within the target disk increases, so do the slopes of these linear fits.

findings.mechanism: Metelli's model predicts independence of transmittance from mean luminance
findings.quote: This solution predicts that the transmittance matches... should be independent of mean luminance.

findings.mechanism: transformation to Michelson contrast makes the data independent of mean luminance, suggesting Michelson contrast is the critical variable
findings.quote: each of the data curves becomes essentially independent of mean luminance.

findings.antecedent: Michelson contrast in the region of transparency
findings.mechanism: visual system uses Michelson contrast to assign surface transmittance
findings.quote: the critical variable that the visual system uses to assign surface transmittance is Michelson contrast, not luminance range.

findings.antecedent: black episcotister (vs white episcotister with same physical transmittance)
findings.mechanism: black episcotister generates a higher Michelson contrast, explaining Metelli's puzzle
findings.quote: the black episcotister generates a higher Michelson contrast than the white one.

findings.mechanism: asymmetry in visual system's processing of transparency
findings.quote: Observers systematically overestimate the transmittance of darkening transparent surfaces

findings.mechanism: asymmetry in visual system's processing of transparency
findings.quote: they systematically underestimate the transmittance of lightening transparent surfaces.

findings.antecedent: transparent surface physical attributes AND occluded surface attributes
findings.mechanism: visual system integrates contextual information for transmittance perception
findings.quote: the perceived transmittance of a transparent surface depends not only on its own physical attributes but also on those of the surface it partially occludes.

findings.mechanism: task requires more variables to be taken into account
findings.quote: Observers reported the lightness-matching task to be much less natural and substantially more difficult.

findings.mechanism: task difficulty leads to strategic influences
findings.quote: the lightness matches exhibit a fair degree of variability across observers.

findings.mechanism: Observer M.S. shows some degree of convergence towards the mean luminance of the surround, indicating partial discounting
findings.quote: matches of Observer M.S. exhibit some degree of convergence toward the mean luminance of the surround, with increasing luminance range within the matching disk.

findings.mechanism: Metelli's model predicts linear functions with specific slopes for lightness matches
findings.quote: The iso-lightness curves are thus predicted to be linear functions with slopes (Amean - Lmean)/(Arange - Lrange).

findings.mechanism: observed lightness matches are a compromise between full and no discounting, not fully predicted by Metelli's T
findings.quote: observers' lightness matches are largely a compromise between these two predictions.

findings.mechanism: observed matches show less convergence (stronger bias toward vertical) than predicted by Metelli's T
findings.quote: strong bias toward the vertical, relative to the predictions based on Metelli's solution for T

findings.consequent: discounting of underlying surface contribution to lightness
findings.mechanism: observers are able to separate and discount only incompletely the contributions of the underlying surface
findings.quote: observers are able to separate and "discount" only incompletely the contributions of the underlying surface

findings.mechanism: effective luminance fails to capture the qualitative trend in the lightness-matching data
findings.quote: effective luminance fails to capture even the qualitative trend in the lightness-matching data

findings.antecedent: luminance range lowered AND Michelson contrast increased (R-C+ regime)
findings.mechanism: visual system does not perceive transparency in R-C+ regime, contradicting Metelli's magnitude constraint
findings.quote: observers do not see the central region as transparent in the regime R-C+ even though the luminance range is lowered.

findings.antecedent: Michelson contrast within central disk (relative to surround)
findings.mechanism: transparency is perceived when Michelson contrast is lowered, supporting a new perceptual theory
findings.quote: observers see transparency when the Michelson contrast within the central disk is lower than in the surround and fail to see transparency otherwise.

findings.antecedent: lightening filters (mean luminance of central disk > surround)
findings.mechanism: asymmetry in visual system's processing of transparency
findings.quote: For lightening filters... the decision as to whether or not the central region is transparent was considerably more difficult.

findings.consequent: zone of confusion OR error bars in transparency judgments
findings.mechanism: asymmetry in visual system's processing of transparency
findings.quote: the data curves for the two tasks are either considerably more separated... or else the data exhibit considerably larger error bars

findings.mechanism: visual system integrates blur as a cue for transparency, relaxing strict textural continuity
findings.quote: observers still perceive transparency in this display... even though the textures in the center and surround are not continuous

findings.mechanism: re-interpretation of contrast-contrast as a transparency phenomenon
findings.quote: the central regions in Figure 20, a and c, appear as transparent disks overlying high-contrast backgrounds

findings.mechanism: lateral inhibition predicts the opposite effect for White's illusion
findings.quote: lateral inhibition would predict that the patches at the bottom should appear to have lower contrast. The perceived effect, however, is just the opposite

findings.mechanism: scission account correctly predicts the sign of White's illusion, unlike lateral inhibition
findings.quote: a scission account predicts not only the correct sign but also certain aspects of the size of the illusion

findings.mechanism: part of the lightness is attributed to the underlying white disks when seen as transparent
findings.quote: the diamond appears darker when it is seen as a transparent surface than when it is seen as an opaque surface.

findings.antecedent: violations of Metelli's constraints 1 & 2 (on alpha, from Beck et al., 1984)
findings.mechanism: Metelli's constraints on alpha are important for visual integration of transparency
findings.quote: Beck et al. (1984)... concluded that violations of the two qualitative constraints based on the restriction 0 < a < 1... adversely affect the perception of transparency

findings.antecedent: violations of Metelli's constraints 3 & 4 (on t, from Beck et al., 1984)
findings.mechanism: Metelli's constraints on t do not hinder transparency perception
findings.quote: violations of the qualitative constraints derived from the restriction 0 < t < 1... do not hinder the perception of transparency

findings.mechanism: Metelli's magnitude constraint is not predictive of perceived transparency
findings.quote: we found in Experiment 3 that Metelli's second qualitative constraint (the magnitude constraint) is not predictive of perceived transparency.

findings.antecedent: equiluminant convergence and translation in color space (D'Zmura et al., 1997)
findings.mechanism: color shifts can elicit transparency even if not physically realizable, indicating a perceptual mechanism
findings.quote: equiluminant convergence and translation in color space can also elicit an impression of transparency

findings.antecedent: convergence model prediction (color space, Chen & D'Zmura, 1998)
findings.mechanism: observers' settings largely conform to the convergence model in color space
findings.quote: For the most part, observers' settings conformed to this prediction.

findings.antecedent: complementary hues (predicted by convergence model, Chen & D'Zmura, 1998)
findings.mechanism: observers avoid complementary hues, indicating a constraint on color integration for transparency
findings.quote: observers avoided settings that led the two halves of the central region to have complementary hues

findings.antecedent: perceptually non-uniform regions of color space (Chen & D'Zmura, 1998)
findings.mechanism: perceptual non-uniformity affects color integration for transparency
findings.quote: observers' settings deviated from the predictions of the convergence model in regions of color space that are perceptually non-uniform

findings.mechanism: perceived color contrast is the critical variable for computing perceptual transparency
findings.quote: perceived color contrast... is the critical variable that the visual system uses to compute perceptual transparency.

findings.antecedent: convergence model (4 parameters) vs affine model (12 parameters) (D'Zmura et al., 2000)
findings.mechanism: convergence model provides a parsimonious fit for color transparency
findings.quote: the convergence model with only 4 parameters... fit the data almost as well as the full affine model with 12 parameters.

findings.mechanism: visual system underestimates transmittance, indicating a bias in visual integration
findings.quote: observers underestimate the transmittance of the filter by a factor of almost two

findings.antecedent: extent to which transparent layer changes mean luminance of underlying surface
findings.mechanism: the bias in perceived transmittance is proportional to the luminance change introduced by the transparent layer
findings.quote: the magnitude of this deviation... is directly proportional to the extent to which the transparent layer changes the mean luminance projected from the underlying surface.

findings.antecedent: intervening transparent layer (D'Zmura et al., 2000, and Exp 2)
findings.mechanism: observers can only partially discount color shifts, indicating limits of visual integration
findings.quote: observers can discount only partially the color shifts introduced by the presence of an intervening transparent layer.

stimuli.description: Large circular disk with vertically oriented sinusoidal grating background, smaller disk inside (target disk) with lower contrast and near disparity. Matching display was identical but adjustable.
Four-intensity displays (Metelli's episcotister model) with bipartite background and central disk, some violating polarity or magnitude constraints.
Examples of unbalanced transparency with inhomogeneous transmittance and lightness.
Figural conditions for transparency, including disruptions in contour continuity.
Junction classification schemes (Z, C, criss-cross configurations) based on Metelli's polarity constraint.
T-junctions and X-junctions demonstrating Anderson's qualitative rule and contrast definitions.
Textured displays with low-contrast image regions, some with textural continuity, some with non-generic alignments, and some with blurring effects from translucent layers.
Contrast-contrast displays with texture patches surrounded by high- or low-contrast textures.
Second-order White's illusion and standard White's illusion displays.
Stereogram demonstrating the effect of perceived transparency on brightness (diamond seen as transparent or opaque over disks).

tables.description: Summary of linear model fits for perceived transmittance matches in Experiment 1 for 3 observers across different target contrasts.
Predicted and observed slopes for lightness matches in Experiment 2 for 3 observers across different target mean luminances.

limitations: The lightness-matching task was reported to be much less natural and substantially more difficult, leading to higher variability across observers and being more prone to strategic influences.
The increased difficulty in estimating the lightness of a transparent surface is attributed to the greater number of variables that must be taken into account in its computation.
